summary: Base64 padding mismatch causes idempotency dedupe to fail across edge routing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer StreamlineAI reports that when their orchestration layer issues repeated calls with the same idempotency token, some retries are still resulting in duplicate tool/function execution. This only occurs intermittently and appears correlated with requests that transit our edge routing layer through the customer's multi-tenant proxy.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream tool executions causing duplicate side-effects (webhook POSTs, job enqueues) for ~0.3% of requests during a burst window.
- Affected a single high-throughput customer on a Dedicated plan.

Environment:
- Platform: Dedicated cluster (us-east), API ingested through edge-proxy -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- SDKs observed: Python (client v1.12.0), Go (client v0.9.4), TypeScript (client v1.8.1) via orchestration service
- Orchestration layer: customer-supplied router that signs idempotency tokens with HMAC-SHA256 and base64-url encodes without padding

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) SDK generates idempotency_token (base64-encoded random nonce, padded) and includes in X-Idempotency-Token header.
2) Customer edge proxy strips trailing '=' padding from header value for routing normalization.
3) Request reaches Redwood api-gateway which does dedup by exact-string match of token header.
4) When a retry arrives with the original padded token (client retries before proxy normalization) or with unpadded value (after proxy normalization), tokens do not match and dedupe fails.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate tool invocation recorded in logs (two separate request IDs) for retries when token normalization differs between client and proxy.

Expected behavior:
- Idempotency dedupe should be resilient to common transport-level normalizations (e.g., base64 padding removal) when the logical token content is identical.

Relevant logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Request A header: X-Idempotency-Token: "Q2hhbGxlbmdlMTIzNA=="
- Request B header seen at edge-proxy: "Q2hhbGxlbmdlMTIzNA" (padding removed)
- Two separate request IDs in Redwood logs: req-az1-00234 and req-az1-00235 both executed function: inventory_reserve

Notes: customer also forwarded packet captures and edge-proxy config showing a header normalization rule that trims '=' characters for indexing purposes.
comments: 2026-03-12 - StreamlineAI (support@streamline.ai): We're seeing occasional double-posts to our inventory webhook. We only retry on 5xx and we attach the same idempotency token. Can you confirm if the platform canonicalizes tokens?

2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks — acknowledging receipt. Assigning to runtime/SRE to investigate possible header normalization during edge routing. Please provide a sample of the raw headers and request IDs (you included those, good).

2026-03-13 - SRE (Diego Ramirez): Preliminary finding: api-gateway performs exact string compare on X-Idempotency-Token. Edge-proxy is indeed trimming '=' in some routing configs. Reproduced locally by sending padded and unpadded tokens — dedupe fails.

2026-03-13 - SDK Eng (Riley Chen): SDKs currently emit base64 with standard padding in Python/Go/TS clients. We should either normalize client-side to unpadded base64-url or server-side to canonical decode/re-encode. Preparing PRs for both approaches.

2026-03-14 - Morgan Lee (Assignee): Action plan: 1) short-term workaround: advise customer to disable header trimming or use the idempotency_token request body field; 2) medium-term: server canonicalization change (decode/normalize) + SDK opt-in change. Rolling patch scheduled for 2026-03-14 to infra edge and SDK releases next week.
2026-03-14 - StreamlineAI (support@streamline.ai): We'll toggle the header rule this afternoon and monitor. Appreciate the quick triage.
investigation:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-12: Issue reported by StreamlineAI; support triaged and SRE looped in.
- 2026-03-12: Customer provided three request IDs and header captures.
- 2026-03-13: SRE reproduced mismatch in staging using edge-proxy header rewrite rule. Exact-string compare on gateway causes dedupe miss.
- 2026-03-13: SDK team confirmed clients produce padded base64; customer proxy strips padding for their routing keys.
- 2026-03-14: Decided dual approach: server-side canonicalization to be highest priority; SDK minor update to produce padding-free urlsafe base64 as an opt-in to reduce chances of mismatch.
Key findings:
- Root cause: token normalization divergence: some proxies remove '=' padding from base64 tokens which changes the header string used for exact matching.
- Frequency: ~0.3% of calls during peak for this customer; reproducible when edge-proxy rule is enabled.
- Risk profile: medium — duplicates cause side-effects but limited to customers with similar proxies.
Evidence and artifacts:
- Repro script attached by SRE (internal).
- Packet captures and gateway logs referenced in related_confluence_pages.

Proposed technical options considered:
- Server-side: canonicalize by base64-decoding header value then re-encoding to a canonical representation (recommended).
- Server-side alternative: accept both padded and unpadded by normalizing on ingress (also acceptable).
- Client-side: update SDKs to emit url-safe unpadded base64 by default (less invasive but requires rollouts).
resolution:
Short-term workaround (2026-03-14):
- Support recommended customer disable the header-trimming rule. Customer applied change and reported reduction in duplicates within 2 hours.

Medium-term fix (deployed 2026-03-14):
- Infra change: api-gateway updated to canonicalize incoming X-Idempotency-Token values by attempting base64 decode and re-encoding to urlsafe unpadded form before dedupe compare. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-edge-proxy/pull/21
- SDK changes: Opt-in flag added to Python/Go/TS clients to emit idempotency tokens using urlsafe unpadded base64; PRs opened and scheduled for release: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/342, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/89
- Rollout notes: Gateway change rolled to us-east first, monitored for 48h for regressions. No new failures observed in the rollout window.

Follow-ups / recommendations to customer:
- Prefer the explicit idempotency_token request field when possible (survives proxy rewriting better than custom headers in some setups).
- If customer must use headers, ensure intermediate proxies preserve header character set (avoid trimming '=').

Post-incident tasks opened:
- INT-9421: Add canonicalization unit tests for header decode/re-encode paths (assigned to infra).
- INT-9432: Update SDK default behavior to urlsafe unpadded base64 after compatibility window (assigned to SDK team).

Status: Fix deployed at gateway and customer confirmed immediate improvement. Multi-SDK releases scheduled next week to reduce client-side exposure.
